parts.title: My noisy neighbour
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
For two months, the flat above mine was empty, and I enjoyed the silence. Then a young man moved in, and everything changed. Every evening at about eleven, I heard loud music through the ceiling, and sometimes I even heard him singing.

At first, I was too shy to complain. I put a pillow over my head and hoped that he would stop. After a week, I was so tired at work that my boss asked if I was ill. I decided that I had to do something.

One Saturday, I knocked on his door, feeling very nervous. To my surprise, he was extremely polite. He told me that he was a night-shift nurse and that he played music to relax when he came home, but he had not realised that the walls were so thin. He apologised several times and promised to use headphones.

Since then, we have become friends. Last week, he brought me a cake as a thank-you, and I invited him for dinner. It is funny to think that I nearly wrote an angry letter instead.

questions.prompt: What changed when the young man moved in?
options: There was loud music at night
The writer found a new job
questions.explanation: Every evening she heard loud music through the ceiling.

questions.prompt: Why didn't the writer complain at first?
questions.explanation: She says she was too shy to complain.

questions.prompt: What made the writer decide to act?
questions.explanation: She was so tired at work that her boss asked if she was ill.

questions.prompt: Why did the neighbour play music?
questions.explanation: He played music to relax when he came home from his night shift.

questions.prompt: How did the story end?
questions.explanation: They became friends, and he brought her a cake.

parts.title: Moving to a new neighbourhood
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
When my family moved to the town of Millbrook last year, I was very sad to leave my old friends. [1] Our new street looked quiet and a little boring, and I wondered how I would ever be happy there.

On our first Saturday, the family next door knocked on our door. [2] They brought a plate of home-made biscuits and a map of the area with their favourite places marked on it. Their daughter, Jess, was the same age as me, and she offered to show me around.

Jess took me to the park, the library and a small café. [3] By the end of the afternoon, I had met six people, and I could remember most of their names. I realised that Millbrook was not as boring as I had expected.

Now, a year later, I feel completely at home. [4] On Friday evenings, a group of us play football in the park, and in summer we all have a barbecue in Jess's garden. [5] I still miss my old friends, but I am grateful that moving brought me so many new ones.
sentences: Her father works at the town hospital.
Jess's brother plays the guitar in a band.
I know almost everyone in our street now.
It is strange to think that I did not want to come here.
Later that week, a van arrived with the rest of our furniture.
They had come to welcome us to the street.
Everything in town was unfamiliar, and I did not know a single person.
The owner smiled at Jess and introduced me to everyone in the café.

gaps.explanation: "Unfamiliar" explains why the town felt boring and the street looked dull.
"They had come to welcome us" explains why the neighbours knocked and brought biscuits.
The owner introduced her to people, which leads to "met six people".
Knowing everyone in the street leads to the football and barbecue examples.
"I did not want to come" contrasts with the happy ending and the sentence "I still miss my old friends".

parts.title: A note to the neighbours
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Dear neighbours, We are having a small party next Saturday evening for our daughter's birthday. We are sorry in advance [1] the noise, so please [2] us know if it disturbs you. The party will [3] at about eleven o'clock. If you [4] like to join us, you are very welcome. We have [5] bought enough food for everyone. We look forward to [6] you there!

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: "Sorry for the noise" is the usual phrase.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: "Let us know" means to inform us.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: After "will" we use the basic form of the verb.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: "If you would like to" is a polite invitation.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "Already bought" shows that the food is ready before the party.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: "Look forward to" is followed by the -ing form.

parts.title: Our community garden
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Our neighbourhood needs your help! The community garden on Elm Street is [1] longer used because the gate is broken. We are asking everybody who lives [2] the area to give a little time. Some neighbours [3] already painted the fence, and it looks lovely. If you [4] free on Saturday morning, please come and join us. You do not have to be good [5] gardening: we will show you what to do. Tea and cake [6] be provided for all the helpers.

gaps.explanation: "Have already painted" is the present perfect: the work is finished and the fence looks lovely now.
"If you are free" is a condition about being available.
"Will be provided" is a promise about the future.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Eugene, do you know when the recycling gets collected this week?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Usually on Mondays, isn’t it? I put mine out on Sunday night.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Me too, but the lorry never came. I phoned the council. They said that because of the holiday it moves to Thursday.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Next Thursday? That’s almost a week away.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: No, this one, so you’ve got two days. Next Thursday is the garden waste.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Oh good, I didn’t want my bin to smell for a week. Thanks.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: No problem. I’ll remind the neighbours too.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Great, see you later.

question.prompt: When is the next recycling collection?
question.explanation: Monday is past because the lorry did not come, and next Thursday is the garden waste; it is moved to this Thursday.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Fiona, I need to clean the gutters. Could I borrow your ladder?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Of course. I can bring it this morning, on my way to the shops.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: That’s kind, but I’m not at home until twelve. I’m playing tennis.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Then tomorrow? I could leave it by your gate.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Tomorrow is too late. It’s going to rain and the gutters will be full. Can you do it today?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Okay, I’ll come with it when I’ve had lunch, at about two.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Perfect. I’ll make you a cup of tea.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Lovely. See you then.

question.prompt: When will the woman bring the ladder?
question.explanation: This morning is when he is out at tennis and tomorrow is too late because of the rain, so she will come after lunch.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Hi, it’s Winona from next door. I talked to our neighbour about his dog, the one that keeps getting into your garden. First he said he’d build a new fence, but then he found out it costs eight hundred pounds, so he changed his mind. He even joked that he’d move to a house with a bigger garden, but he loves this street too much. In the end he will keep the dog inside the house during the day and take it for walks in the park instead. So you shouldn’t have any more problems. Call me if there’s anything else.

question.explanation: The fence is too expensive and the move was a joke; he will keep the dog inside the house during the day.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Hi Clover, you asked me where the post office is. Most people will tell you it’s opposite the bakery, but that was the old one, and it closed in the spring. The new one is on High Street, right beside the bank, with a blue sign. I thought of the library too, because they used to sell stamps at a small desk, but that stopped in the summer. So walk straight on, turn left at the traffic lights, and you’ll see it on your right. It closes at five, so don’t be late. Hope that helps!

question.explanation: The bakery post office closed and the library desk stopped; the new one is beside the bank.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Hi Roland, it’s Eilidh about Saturday’s meeting. The tickets will be sold at the door by Mrs Pryce, so you don’t need to collect them. And I know that last time you made the tea, but a new volunteer wants to do it this time. What I’d like is for you to come at half past five instead of six. The hall is full of boxes and we need to put out a hundred chairs before people arrive. Thanks so much. Call me if you can’t make it.

question.prompt: Why should the man arrive early?
question.explanation: Mrs Pryce sells the tickets and a new volunteer makes the tea; Eilidh needs him early to put out a hundred chairs.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Cormac, I hear you’re selling your house.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Yes, after thirty years. The children have all left, and now it’s just me and the cat. Six bedrooms is silly.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Is it the noise? The road is so busy.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Not really. I stopped hearing it years ago.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Or is it too far from the town centre?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: A bit, but I have a car, and I like the quiet. No, I want a flat where I only need to clean two rooms.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That makes sense. Where will you go?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Somewhere near the park, I hope.

question.prompt: Why is the man selling his house?
options: It is too large for him now
It is too noisy for him
It is too far from town
question.explanation: The noise does not bother him and the distance is not a problem; with the children gone he finds six bedrooms silly.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Madge, I’d like to rent the flat on Park Road. How much is it?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: The rent is six hundred pounds a month.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Is that all? I thought the owner wanted more.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Water and heating are another fifty, and everyone pays them. Add that to the rent and you have the figure for the form.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: What about the parking space? I saw a sign on the gate.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That’s another fifty, so seven hundred pounds in total. But you don’t have a car, do you?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: No, I come to work by bike, so I won’t need it.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Good, then I’ll prepare the contract.

question.prompt: How much will the man pay each month in total?
question.explanation: The rent is six hundred and the bills add fifty; seven hundred would include a parking space that he does not need.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Osian, my car’s in the garage until Friday. How are you getting to work?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I usually go by bus, but it takes an hour with all the changes.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Same for me. What about getting a lift from Dan in your office?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: He lives in the opposite direction. He’d have to drive for an hour to pick me up.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Right. What about a taxi? It’s expensive alone, but if we split it...

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: It would be about ten pounds each. That’s cheaper than I thought, and we’d be there in twenty minutes.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: And we could leave later.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Brilliant. I’ll book it for Monday.

question.explanation: The bus takes an hour and Dan lives too far away, so they agree to split the cost of a taxi.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Hi Holly, you look happy. What’s up?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I just walked past the new shop on Mill Street, the one that sells fruit and vegetables from local farms.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Is it expensive? New shops usually are.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That’s what I thought, but it’s cheaper than the supermarket.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: And is it far from here?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Just five minutes. Honestly, the street needed something like this. The old empty shop was so depressing.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I might go on Saturday.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Do! You’ll love it. They even gave me a free apple to try, and the man behind the counter was really friendly.

question.prompt: What does Holly think of the new shop?
options: It is just what the street needed
It is too far to walk
question.explanation: It is cheaper than the supermarket and only five minutes away; she says the street needed something like it.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Cora, are you busy next week? I need a favour.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Of course. Do you want me to cut your grass? It looked very long.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: A neighbour’s son does that, thanks. And I’m taking the car to be washed on my way to the airport.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: So what, then?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’m away for ten days, and my cat hates the cattery. Could you come twice a day with food? It’s a bit of a job, I know.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I don’t mind at all, I love cats.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: You’re a star. I’ll leave the key under the pot.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Perfect.

question.prompt: What does the man want her to do?
question.explanation: The grass and the car are already organised; he is away and needs someone to look after his cat.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Lukas, have you thought more about the street party?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Yes. I’d like to use the school hall in case it rains.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: That’s sensible, but the hall costs eighty pounds. We’ve only got fifty, and the street is free.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Okay, we’ll risk the street. Should we move it to a Sunday?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: No, Saturday works. The council only lends us the tables on Saturdays. The real problem is that only five people have offered to help, and we expect a hundred guests.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: You’re right. That worries me more than the weather.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Let’s ask the neighbours this week.

question.prompt: What do Bea and Lukas agree about the street party?
options: It should be in the school hall
It should be on a Sunday
question.explanation: The hall is too expensive and Saturday is the day for the tables; both are worried that only five people will help.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Good afternoon, I’m Officer Penn. I’m visiting all the houses in the street today.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Oh dear, is something wrong?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Nothing serious. I’m not here to take a statement or anything. There have been a few bicycle thefts, so I’m giving people some tips.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Right. We keep our bikes in the garden.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I’d suggest locking them to something solid, even in the garden, and writing down the number on the frame.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I never thought of that. Is there a charge for the leaflet?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: No, it’s free. Here you are.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Thank you very much.

question.prompt: What is the police officer doing?
question.explanation: He says it is not a statement and the leaflet is free; he is visiting houses to give tips about bicycle thefts.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Oh, hi Farid! What a surprise.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Sorry to bother you. I wanted to borrow your drill, but I found one in my garage, so never mind.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Do you want some sugar, then? I know you were out yesterday.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: No, I’m fine. The reason I’m here is this parcel. The postman left it with me by mistake. It has your name on it.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Oh, thank you. I’ve been waiting for it for a week!

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: No problem. I thought you’d be worried.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I was. Come in for a coffee?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Maybe another day.

question.prompt: Why is the man at the door?
question.explanation: He no longer needs the drill and does not want sugar; he brings her parcel that the postman left with him.

parts.title: Welcome to the community centre
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: gillian
turns.text: Good morning, and welcome to the Oakfield Community Centre. My name is Gillian. We are open from nine in the morning until ten at night, six days a week. The centre used to be closed on Sundays, but we changed that last year, because so many people wanted to come at weekends. Now we close on Mondays, when the cleaners and the gardeners work. Let me tell you about the café. It’s on the ground floor. Coffee is two pounds, but if you prefer tea, it’s only one pound, and a biscuit is fifty pence. Next, classes. Many people ask about the dance class, which is on Wednesdays and costs five pounds. The class that doesn’t cost anything is yoga, on Tuesdays at ten. It’s very popular, so please arrive early. Then the art club. It’s for children and adults. It used to meet at three, but too many children were still at school, so now it starts at four o’clock. You can bring your own paints, but we have some for you. Now, some of you will want to hold a party or a meeting. The small room costs twenty pounds, but the big hall, which holds a hundred people, costs forty pounds for an afternoon. You can pay at the office or online. Finally, volunteers. We always need help with the café and the garden. Please don’t speak to the manager, Mr Hill, because he is very busy. Mrs Dunn organises the volunteers, and she is in the office every morning. That’s D, U, N, N. If you have any questions, ask at the desk by the front door, or look at the board in the entrance, where we put all the news. Thank you for listening, and enjoy the centre.

gaps.prompt: The centre does not open on ___
gaps.explanation: They used to close on Sundays, but now it is Monday.

gaps.prompt: In the café, a cup of tea costs ___ pound
gaps.explanation: Coffee is two pounds, but tea is one pound.

gaps.prompt: There is no charge for ___ lessons on Tuesdays
gaps.explanation: Dance costs five pounds on Wednesdays; the class that is free is yoga on Tuesdays.

gaps.prompt: Children's art club starts at ___ o'clock
gaps.explanation: It used to meet at three, but now it starts at four.

gaps.prompt: The big hall can be rented for ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: The small room is twenty pounds; the big hall is forty.
She does not say Mr Hill; Mrs Dunn organises the volunteers.

parts.title: A community worker
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: Donna, why did you become a community worker?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: People expect me to say I lost my first job. I did, a shop job, but I found another one within a month. And a teacher at school did suggest it once, but I just laughed at her. The real reason is that I moved to the city for work and I missed my old neighbourhood, where everybody knew everybody. I wanted to build that feeling again here, and my family thought I was a little crazy.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: What do you organise?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: Football matches were my first idea, but only a few boys came, so we stopped. We do one coach trip to the seaside in the summer, but that’s only once a year. The main things are lunches on Wednesdays, where people cook together, and repair days once a month, when neighbours fix bikes, radios and clothes.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: What do you think is the biggest problem?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: Prices are going up, and everybody complains about it, but I can’t do much about that. The streets are noisy at weekends too, but people get used to it. What worries me most is loneliness. Older people can go a week without talking to anybody, and they never tell you, because they’re too polite.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: What has worked best?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: We tried a monthly newspaper, but it took too many hours to write and nobody read all of it. A telephone line was fine, but people prefer to talk face to face. The surprise success is a big wall at the community centre where everybody leaves notes, offers and thank-you messages. It costs nothing, it is always full, and people sometimes answer each other’s notes, which I love to see.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: How did you feel about the goat at the last street party?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: The rain was forecast, but it stayed dry, and the music was loud, but we had permission. Then a man arrived with a goat! I thought, oh no, everyone will complain, and I felt a bit nervous. But the children loved it and I couldn’t stop laughing. I wasn’t angry, and the owner is a lovely man.

turns.speaker: mitchell
turns.text: What will you open next year?

turns.speaker: fatima
turns.text: People keep asking for a small café, and I’d love one, but we can’t afford the rent yet. The council suggested a second office, but we don’t really need it. What we are going to do is a tool library, where people can borrow drills and ladders for a small deposit.

questions.prompt: Why did Donna want to become a community worker?
questions.explanation: The job loss and the teacher were not the reason; she missed her old neighbourhood where everybody knew everybody.

questions.prompt: What does she organise?
questions.explanation: Football stopped and the coach trip is once a year; the main events are lunches and repair days.

questions.prompt: What does she think is the biggest problem?
questions.explanation: She says prices and noise are not what worries her most; she is most worried about older people who feel lonely.

questions.prompt: What has worked best?
questions.explanation: The newspaper took too many hours and the telephone line was only fine; the wall for messages was the surprise success.

questions.prompt: How did Donna feel about the goat at the last street party?
options: Embarrassed in front of the guests
questions.explanation: She was nervous at first, but the children loved it and she could not stop laughing; she was not angry.

questions.prompt: What will she open?
questions.explanation: A café costs too much rent and a second office is not needed; they will open a place to borrow drills and ladders.

parts.title: Describe a photograph
